answer.rationale: Rollback is ruled out by compliance on the security patch. Regional failover has no current signal that the issue is regional; write-path p99 with heavy settlement writes points to primary DB contention, not regional routing. Add capacity can't be provisioned and validated inside one intervention window at peak. Circuit breaker on a dependency would shed legitimate settlement writes at peak - exactly the writes the objective is to preserve. Routing read replica traffic off the primary is the only intervention that: (a) relieves write-path pressure without reverting the must-keep security patch, (b) does not shed writes, and (c) is supported by direct precedent. Memory_b5 describes exactly this intervention working before: routing read traffic to read replicas took dashboard/secondary read load off the primary and write latency recovered the same day. I'm verifying that one memory to confirm the prior pattern (which replica set, what shift was safe, what recovery looked like) before committing.
